'''Fiona J. Burnell''' (born 1979){{r|loc}} is a Canadian-American [[condensed matter physics|condensed matter physicist]] who studies [[State of matter|exotic states of matter]] including [[Fractional quantum Hall effect|fractional quantum Hall states]] and [[topological insulator]]s.{{r|shape}} She is Tang Family Professor in the School of Physics and Astronomy at the [[University of Minnesota]],{{r|tang}} and a quondam fellow of [[All Souls College, Oxford]].{{r|asc}}

==Education and career==
Burnell graduated from the [[University of British Columbia]] in 2002, and received a Ph.D. from [[Princeton University]] in 2009.{{r|profile}} At Princeton, she was a student of [[Shivaji Sondhi]].{{r|sondhi}} Her dissertation was ''On exotic orders in strongly correlated systems''.{{r|diss}}

She was a postdoctoral researcher at All Souls College from 2009 to 2013,{{r|profile}} and continues to be listed as a quondam fellow at All Souls.{{r|asc}} She joined the University of Minnesota in 2013;{{r|welcome}} she became a full professor, and was appointed as the inaugural Tang Family Professor, in 2024.{{r|tang}}

==Recognition==
Burnell was named as a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] (APS) in 2023, after a nomination from the APS Division of Condensed Matter Physics, "for outstanding contributions toward the elucidation of exotic phases of matter, including topological phases that are not described by the conventional Landau classification based on broken symmetries".{{r|faps}}
